# ASL Rule Inventory: Chapters A to E

**Status:** First made 2026-10-05, of `main` at 16fb5f0. A working document: a pass that builds a rule changes its row here, as it changes the section's row in the [ASL Rule Coverage](<ASL Rule Coverage.md>). Since 2026-10-28 it is becoming the one ledger of the [Rules-first four-track plan](<Plans/ASL Rules-First Four-Track Plan.md>) (its Step 0): the Rules calculator column, the Turns work, and the Owner, Claim state, and Minigames columns are in (section 3), and the rows beyond Chapter E (section 1, point 5), with the counts written by script. The file keeps its name until a rename, which goes by pull request.

**What it is.** One row for every numbered rule of Chapters A to E of the registered rulebook (eASLRB v3.01), and since 2026-10-28 of F, G, H1, W, and the ASOP, not yet audited (section 1, point 5): its title, the physical page of the PDF it is printed on, its status in the code, where the code is, and the pass of the [redesign plan](<ASL Card Play and Map Studio Redesign Plan.md>), section 22.1, that takes it, or the ruling that leaves it out. Section 22.1 is provisionally approved (the user, 2026-10-05) and is the schedule in force since 2026-10-09 (the plan's section 23). The passes were renumbered that day in the order they run, in steps of five (the plan's section 4 has the table of old and new numbers).

## 1. How it was made

1. **The list of rules comes from the PDF.** The PDF's own outline gave 2,058 numbered entries for pages 43 to 253. A script then read every page's text layer for rule heads (a bold number at the start of a paragraph) and compared. That added 71 rules the outline lacks, removed nothing, and corrected the outline in the places section 5 lists. The page in each row is the page the rule's head is printed on.
2. **Each rule was read on its PDF page and judged against the code and the tests** by 19 read-only audits, one for each group of sections, each working from the PDF's page text (and from rendered pages where a table or figure carried the rule). The repository's transcription was a search aid only.
3. **I checked myself** what the pass assignments and the counts rest on. The rows marked "me" in the last column are the ones where I read the rule's text in the PDF and the code: A.8, A7.21, A16, A17.11, A19.12, A25.2, B1.14, B1.16, B14.4, B16.21, D2.16, and the thirteen rows of D17. I also read in the PDF, without tracing all the code: A.18, A8.2, A8.23, A7.9, A10.533, A11.11, B25.14, C10.1, E.1, and the optional-rule marks of A7.37, B10.211, C13.311, and D11.1. Every other status is an audit's, taken as reported. Every title and page is mine, by script.
4. **No test was run and nothing was built.** "Built" means logic and a test that reaches it were found by reading. Several audits named tests from their method names without opening them; their findings files say which.
5. **The rows beyond Chapter E** (Step 0 of the [Rules-first four-track plan](<Plans/ASL Rules-First Four-Track Plan.md>), question 8, 2026-10-28) were made the same way, by script (`code-builders/pass-history/step0-inventory-ledger/rows_beyond_e.py`), from the same PDF (eASLRB v3.01): the outline's entries for F (pp. 254 to 270), G (pp. 276 to 322), H1, the DYO purchase (pp. 328 to 335), and W (pp. 656 to 669), compared with the rule heads printed on those pages. The heads added ten rules the outline lacks (F.8E, F5.4252, G8.22, G17.111, G18.1, G18.62, H1.441, H1.49, H1.51, W10.132), moved G15.111 to page 318, where its head is, and read the outline's "W.6BG" as W.6B, as printed; five outline entries keep the outline's page, and their notes say so: G.5 and G2.21, whose heads the text layer runs into the next word; H1.72, whose number is split across two fonts; H1.20, which has no head of its own; and G9.7, whose head was not found on its page. Appendix 2, the ASOP (pp. 678 to 681), has no outline entries: its 120 rows are its printed steps. The chapters' footnotes and tables are not rows. The Chapter H Notes (pp. 336 to 598) get a row each as track 1 brings the counter that carries it into the catalog (question 8); J and K have none. No row beyond E has been audited: each is "not audited", open, and in the claim wave question 8 gives it (the "Pass or ruling" column). G10's rows name the Turns track's calculators.

**Statuses.**

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| built | The rule's mechanics are in the code as the PDF states them, and a test or a clear call path reaches them. |
| built with a deviation | In the code, knowingly different from the rule: a ruling, a simplification, or a choice the game makes for the player. |
| partly | Some of the rule's mechanics are in the code and some are not. The note says which. |
| refused | The game meets the situation and refuses it with a reason. |
| not built | No implementing logic. A counter, a vocabulary word, a card's text, or a comment alone is not built. |
| not applicable | Nothing to implement: a heading with no rule text of its own, a definition, a pointer, or a table procedure the program replaces. |
| not audited | A row beyond Chapter E, added from the PDF on 2026-10-28 (section 1, point 5) and not yet judged against the code. Its claim reads it. |

## 3. Reading the tables

- **§** is the rule's number with its chapter letter. **Page** is the physical page of the PDF.
- **Where** names the file and member that implement or refuse the rule; **Test** a test that reaches it. Both are empty for a rule that is not built or not applicable.
- **Rules calculator** (Step 0 of the [Rules-first four-track plan](<Plans/ASL Rules-First Four-Track Plan.md>), 2026-10-28) names the Rules members that decide the rule. Every ASL rule is decided in the Rules project alone, so a rule decided anywhere else is a fault and a claim. The cell reads:
  - the Rules members alone: Rules decides, and the code outside Rules only gathers facts and writes events;
  - "residual outside Rules: ..." after them: Rules decides part, and the file, lines, and member named still decide a clause of the rule;
  - "none; decided outside Rules: ...": no Rules member decides the rule;
  - "Maps (LOS and range stay in Maps, ruling 2026-10-05)": the decision is LOS or terrain height, which stays in Maps;
  - "none needed: a fact, not a decision": a state default, a catalog value, a check of counter data, or a map fact;
  - "(from Where, not read)": the Rules members the Where cell names, taken by script. These 840 rows were not read for a residual; one found in passing is marked "(found in passing)";
  - "Turns work, task (not read against the PDF): ...": a calculator the Turns track wrote for the rule (the Turn Guide's B5, and the later Rules plan's D1 to D4), recorded on 2026-10-28 without changing the row's status. Where the row already names another Rules member, the rule has two calculators, which its claim reconciles into one (the plan's section 4.4). G10's calculators are recorded when the chapter G rows are added;
  - "none" for a rule not built, and empty for one not applicable.

  The 121 implemented rows whose Where named no Rules code were read on 2026-10-28 (four read-only agents, every residual and every row without a Rules member checked by hand on its lines, and 13 of the others) and their Where cells corrected: most had been written before pass 32 moved the rule into Rules. The script and the agents' findings are in `code-builders/pass-history/step0-inventory-ledger/`.
- **Pass or ruling** is empty for a rule that is built or not applicable.
- **Owner**, **Claim state**, and **Minigames** are the claim board's (the plan's sections 4.2 and 7.1). Owner names the claim and the agent that holds it. Claim state is one of open, claimed, built, reviewed, wired, and accepted, as the plan's section 4.3 defines them. Minigames lists the bundles that prove the rule, written by script from their manifests. On 2026-10-28 every row that carries a rule was set open with no owner: no row has yet been through a claim (a contract, a minigame bundle, its tests, a review), whatever its Status says of the code. A row not applicable has no claim state.
- **By** says who judged the row: "me", or "audit" for one of the 19 audits.

## 5. The PDF, its outline, and the transcription

**The PDF's outline against its pages.** The PDF wins; these are faults of the outline, not of the rules.

- 69 rules are printed on the pages and missing from the outline: A6.8, A7.351, A7.352, A7.353, A7.52, A7.531, A8.21, A11.34, A13.511, A20.24, A23.71, A25.01, A25.111, A25.13, A25.224, A25.242, A25.58, A26.221, B9.33, B16.32, B16.41, B19.21, B20.46, B23.733, B23.911, B23.912, B27.13, B28.52, B31.1411, B32.4, B32.42, B32.43, B32.44, C.5C, C1.733, C3.41, C3.51, C3.52, C3.53, C5.71, C5.72, C6.58, C7.311, C7.321, C7.331, C7.332, C8.92, C9.1, C10.41, C11.51, C12.22, C12.23, C12.24, D4.221, D4.222, D4.223, D6.651, D6.72, D6.83, D8.32, E1.17, E1.23, E2.43, E3.751, E3.752, E8.232, E11.251, E11.255, E11.26.
- 50 rules are printed one page from where the outline points: A25.3, A25.57, A25.6, A25.61, A25.62, A25.63, A25.64, A25.65, A25.66, A25.7, A26.2, B13.81, B13.82, B23.9221, B24.1, B25.1, B25.11, B26.5, B27.5, B28.1, B28.2, B28.3, B28.4, B28.41, B28.411, B28.412, B28.5, B28.51, B29.1, B29.2, B29.3, B29.4, B30.34, B30.35, B30.4, B30.41, B31.121, B33.11, B34.4, B34.41, B34.42, B34.43, B34.5, B34.6, B34.7, B35.1, B35.2, B35.3, E1.921, E1.922.
- The outline numbers B24.72 twice; the second is B24.73 (Wire) on page 142. It lists E3.313 as 3.13. It lists a B16.21 that page 130 does not print. Its "A7.30 Results" is a label over A7.301 to A7.309, not a rule.
- The outline's titles differ from the page in places: C5.64 is OVR PREVENTION (outline: Protection), C7.11 TK# DERIVATION and C7.2 MODIFIED TK# (outline: TH#), C8.4 CANISTER, C8.6 WHITE PHOSPHORUS, C13.9 SHAPED-CHARGE WEAPONS, A25.936 MMG/HMG/MTR (outline: ATR), E11.252 RADIOLESS AFV, E12.4 CORRECTING.
- Two heads are lost from the text layer and were read on the rendered page by the audits: A7.8 PIN (page 58) and D15.1 (page 214).

**The transcription (`docs/ASL/Rulebook_Markdown`) against the PDF.**

- **Page markers.** For 419 rows the transcription's `<!-- page N -->` marker is not the page the rule is printed on (A: 154, B: 88, C: 57, D: 49, E: 71), nearly always one page low: the marker stands where a page's text was placed, and a rule that starts in a page's second column is filed under the page before. A citation's page must come from the PDF, as in this document.
- **Wording and numbers.** Where the audits compared them, the transcription's rule text agreed with the PDF. Two audits compared whole sections sentence by sentence (A10 to A12, and C5 to C9) and found no difference. The others made spot checks. A25 was not compared.
- **Text lost or misplaced in the transcription:** B23.23 has lost its head and most of its rule (page 136). A7.8's opening words are missing, as they are from the PDF's text layer. D17.22 has the Aerosan Movement Table's heading spliced into a word. E1.93's head and B36.1 sit inside code blocks, where a search for a rule head misses them. Line-break hyphens survive inside words ("Infan-try"), which defeats a plain search.
- **Heads my script could not match in the transcription** (26; most are rules set in bold where it looked for a heading, and the outline's own errors): A16, A24.61, A7.30, A7.37, A7.8, B10.21, B10.211, B10.3, B10.31, B10.52, B16.21, B23.23, B31, B32, B33, B34, B35, B36, B36.1, B37, C13.311, C6.521, D11.211, D15.1, D17, E1.93.
- **Chapter D has 17 sections.** D17 Aerosans (pages 216 to 217) is in the PDF and in the transcription. The coverage document of 2026-10-05 had no row for it and counted 104 sections; there are 105.

**E.1 (page 222)** says Chapter E "is composed entirely of Optional rules and SSR": none of it applies unless a card cites it or the players agree. The rows of Chapter E are judged as rules all the same, since the aim is complete coverage of A to E.

## 6. Claims

The claim board of the [Rules-first four-track plan](<Plans/ASL Rules-First Four-Track Plan.md>) (section 4; questions 1 to 3, ruled by the user on 2026-10-28). `AGENTS.md` says how a claim is made, built, and reviewed; `code-builders/documents/claim_check.py` checks this table against the rows' Owner and Claim state cells, in the merge gate's strict stage and in CI.

- **Claim**: its id, the rule section it takes (A10), or a subsection group where the section is large (A7.3); an id that is not a rule section names its work (proving-slice).
- **Agent**: Claude or Codex, the agent that holds it. **Reviewer**: the other agent, or "sub-agent" when only one is working.
- **Branch**: the branch the claim's work is done on.
- **Calculator files**: the files of the Rules project the claim will change, by file name, comma-separated. While the claim is claimed or built it holds them: no other claim may list them, and a branch may change a Rules file only when a claim of that branch lists it. A file written "Name.cs (shared)" is one the claim changes only at its edges (a call into its own calculator, a field on a record); several claims may hold a file shared at once, never when one of them holds it whole (2026-10-29). Files outside the Rules project are not listed: `claim_check.py` warns when two open claims' branches change the same one.
- **State**: claimed, built, reviewed, wired, or accepted (the plan's section 4.3).
- **The batch gate** (the plan's section 4.3, the user, 2026-10-29): a rule claim merges on CI without a gate of its own; after every fifth rule claim merged since the commit below, the merge gate runs on main (`gate.sh rules-batch <commit> baseline`, `build`, `proofs`, `carry`), and the commit it proved replaces the one below. `claim_check.py` counts the merges and holds the next rule claim at five.

**Last batch gate:** `ee967f71` (2026-10-30: the third batch gate, on main after the five claims B (D5.34 with A7.7, B23.74, A20.54, E1.8, C10.3; PR 82); proved against `d0885243`'s carried baseline, made from `f525ea78`: the replay digest and the sweep differ in nothing, the text list only by the new texts (four lines changed their counts only); its baseline carried. `claim_check.py` counts merged claim branches, not claims, so it read this batch as 1 of 5; the board's rule counts claims). The second batch gate was `d0885243` (2026-10-30, on main after the B25.2, A23.3, and five audit-fault claims (A21.13, A10.531, A8.41, A11.17, A11.5) and Codex's D3.7 adapters; proved against `580aadf6`'s carried baseline, made from `f525ea78`: the replay digest and the sweep differ in nothing, the text list only by the new texts; its baseline carried, so the next batch gate needs no base stage. Its first proofs differed in every state: the carried baseline lacked a property the first gate had skipped, and gate.sh now takes the skip list from the commit a carried baseline was made from). The first batch gate was `580aadf6` (2026-10-29), proved against `f525ea78`. Every row the claim owns carries the same state in its Claim state cell, and its Owner cell reads "claim (agent)", for example "C9.3 (Codex)".

## 7. Wiring

The wiring rows of the [Rules-first plan](<Plans/ASL Rules-First Four-Track Plan.md>), section 9.1 (the user, 2026-10-29): what track 3 must move onto a calculator a rule claim built. A rule claim adds its row when it reaches "built"; a wiring claim of section 8 takes it. `code-builders/documents/claim_check.py` checks this table with sections 6 and 8.

- **Wiring**: `W-` and the rule claim's id. **Rule claim**: the claim of section 6 whose calculator is wired. **Capability**: the capability of the plan's section 9 whose wiring claim takes the row (fire, movement, rout, rally, close combat, setup and work, the turn's boundaries).
- **Sites to rewire**: each place outside Rules that decides the rule today, as `file: member`, with the calculator method that replaces it; or a command or read that does not exist yet and must ask the calculator.
- **Old members to remove**: the Rules members that keep their callers' answers until the wiring moves them (the Rules conventions, section 2, step 5).
- **Behavior changes**: what play will allow or refuse differently once wired; each is a named difference at the wiring claim's gate.
- **Owner**: "wiring claim (agent)", blank while open. **State**: open, claimed, wired, reviewed, or accepted; an owned row's state is its wiring claim's.

## 8. Wiring claims

The claims of track 3 (the plan's section 9.1): each takes the open wiring rows of one capability whose rule claims are built. It is made like a rule claim, by one commit to main that adds its row here and fills its wiring rows' Owner and State; the push is the lock.

- **Claim**: `wire-` and its capability, with a number when a capability is wired in parts (`wire-fire-1`). **Agent**, **Reviewer**, **Branch**: as in section 6.
- **Held files**: the files outside Rules it will change, by path under `src/ASL/`, comma-separated, each whole or "(shared)". While the claim is claimed it holds them: no two wiring claims hold one file whole, and its branch changes only those files, their tests, and the Rules members its rows name for removal.
- **Capability**: fire, movement, rout, rally, close combat, setup and work, or the turn's boundaries (the plan's section 9).
- **State**: claimed, wired, reviewed, or accepted. When every wiring row of a rule claim is wired, the rule claim and its rows move to "wired".
